badge: NATIVE INTEGRATIONS, NOT ONE GENERIC ENDPOINT
title: Each provider gets its own adapter
body: Anthropic speaks the Messages API, Gemini uses generateContent, Ollama talks to /api/chat, and local GGUF runs in-process through llama.cpp with no HTTP at all. Aggregators such as OpenRouter, Together AI and Replicate get their own credential scopes and model IDs, while Azure deployments and MiniMax's international and China endpoints are handled separately. Model lists, thinking and image-generation capabilities, and default parameters are detected per provider. OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible endpoints are an extra option for self-hosted services — not a single pipe that every model is forced through.

lede: Everything you need to know about UChat AI.

q: Can I use it without an API key?
a: Yes. Local providers — Ollama, LM Studio and the built-in GGUF engine — run entirely in-process with no API key. Ollama and LM Studio can also point at LAN or remote servers.

q: Where do my API keys live?
a: Your keys are stored on your device and used to talk directly to the provider you choose. UChat AI does not require an account.

title: Not Just Chat. An Agent That Gets Things Done.
lede: UChat AI puts real tools behind the models. Connect remote MCP servers, switch on any of the 12 built-in tools, or let the model run SSH operations on your servers — all inside one native chat window.

title: MCP servers, one click away
body: Add a streamable HTTP MCP server and UChat AI discovers its tools automatically, then hands them to the model alongside the built-in ones. Custom auth headers, per-tool switches, JSON import and automatic reconnect after network changes are all included.

title: 12 built-in tools, on your terms
body: Fetch a URL, query RDAP or exchange rates, check the weather, read system info and time, resolve IPs from an offline GeoLite2 database, generate keys, wake a machine over LAN, or have the model create an image. Every tool is opt-in and stays inside the App Sandbox.

title: A real remote terminal toolkit
body: The SSH tool ships around 30 actions: run remote commands and capture their output, manage files over SFTP, inspect server status and control Docker containers. Credentials stay in the local database, so the model never has to ask for a password.
